title: Latency Origami — morning p99 hunt
content:
Morning dump (short) — focus: follow-up from last night’s p99 surge on small models (gpt-small-ish) when concurrent sessions hit ~1.8k. Goal: triage potential KV cache eviction interplay + hot-key amplification.

Summary / hypothesis:
- Symptoms: sustained p99 increase from ~120ms to 480ms for many short requests (<=16 tokens). 90p/avg mostly stable.
- Hypothesis A: cache churn due to aggressive memory reclaim on a subset of workers + uneven request routing (same user/session bouncing between shards) -> repeated KV cache rebuilds.
- Hypothesis B: hot-key amplification (few prompt prefixes causing large batch formation spikes) pushing some workers into large-batch slow path and blocking smaller fast-path requests.
- Hypothesis C: kernel stall due to mutex contention around LRU bookkeeping in our shard-local cache implementation (observed in similar past incidents).

Quick evidence to collect (start here):
- /var/log/inference-runtime/syslog grep for kvcache-evict events between 2026-03-11T22:00 and 2026-03-12T02:00 on cluster gw-*-pool. Command: sudo journalctl -u inference-runtime --since "2026-03-11 21:30" --until "2026-03-12 02:30" | grep -i kvcache
- Correlate routing: query request_id -> worker_id mapping from trace service for spike window. Use trace-id prefix: spike-20260311-22.
- Dump per-worker batch-size histogram from metrics-store: metric name "runtime.batch.size_per_request" tag model=gpt-small-ish.

Immediate triage steps (today):
- [ ] Run a targeted repro on a staging pool with synthetic hot-prefix traffic (use reproducer script: tools/repro/hotkey_spike.py). Collect perf counters + mutex histograms. (Owner: Amara, ETA EOD)
- [ ] Disable LRU-prefetch optimization on one Canary pool to see regression/amelioration. (Owner: Ethan, ETA today morning)
- [ ] Add short-lived logging around cache.rebuild path (TRACE) gated by env REDWOOD_DEBUG_REBUILD=1 to capture stack traces without noisy always-on logs. (Owner: Amara -> small PR)
- [ ] Patch router to prefer sticky routing for sessions with >5 requests in last 60s as a short mitigation. Quick flag flip for canary. (Owner: Priya)

Observations from quick checks (from last night):
- Kernel logs show repeated "kvcache: evicting 512 entries" from worker-17 that coincides with a tail of CPU 100% for a few seconds. Not every worker evicted; cluster skewed.
- Prometheus snapshot: worker-17 batch size median=8 but p99 batch size=64 for the spike window.
- No OOMs recorded, but mem_free dipped intermittently -> suggests transient GC-like behavior in cache management.

Potential root causes and action riffing:
- If eviction is causal: our eviction threshold is too conservative for small-model memory footprints under bursty access; consider lowering threshold for gpt-small-ish or switching to frequency-based eviction for short sequences. Action: design quick config change that reduces target_cache_size by 15% for canary.
- If routing is causal: introduce session affinity at router level (sticky hash) and measure tail. If improves, roll to more pools.
- If mutex contention: profile using perf + tracepoints; possible fix is to shard LRU locks further or use lock-free approximate LRU (sketch doc: notes/approx-lru-ideas.md).

Notes for PR / experiment checklist:
- Repro script: add random jitter to request inter-arrival to simulate real-world mixing. Ensure we measure both per-request latency and per-token CPU.
- When patching, keep logs gated behind REDWOOD_DEBUG_* and only enable in canary for 2h windows.
- Telemetry to capture: cache.rebuild.count, cache.eviction.size, worker.batch.max, worker.lock.wait_ms (histogram), router.sticky_miss_rate.

Playbook snippets to run now locally (copyable):
- tail logs: sudo journalctl -u inference-runtime -f | grep -E "kvcache|rebuild|evict|batch-size"
- dump metrics for worker-17: curl -s "http://metrics-store.internal/api/v1/query?query=runtime_batch_size%7Bworker%3D\"worker-17\"%7D" | jq .
- perf attach to PID 22411 (worker-17): sudo perf record -F 99 -p 22411 -g -- sleep 30; sudo perf report --no-children | head

Open questions / to decide:
1) Do we prefer quick sticky routing as band-aid or invest in smarter caching policy first? My inclination: sticky routing quick can reduce cross-shard churn immediately.
2) How to instrument LRU contention without adding 2x latency overhead for production? Tracepoints + sampling.
3) Is the small model's quantized KV layout contributing (memory fragmentation)? Need allocator stats.

Things to log to incident page (ENGINF-927) after repro:
- exact commit SHA used on canary
- canary nodes list + DNS names
- repro scripts + parameters
- before/after p99 numbers + raw metric extracts

Personal TODO (post-triage):
- [ ] Draft quick config flag PR for cache size tweak (branch: amara/cache-size-quick)
- [ ] Open follow-up RFC for durable sticky routing policy (link to be created)
- [ ] Add unit test for cache.rebuild to ensure path is bounded in worst-case O(k) where k=entries evicted (avoid accidental quadratic behavior)

Random fwiw (brain soup):
- Consider adding a tiny per-request cookie that encodes last-worker-id and use router to bias next request -> minimal infra change and reversible.
- If we move to frequency-based eviction, watch for cold-start churn when new sessions appear.

Slack pings planned:
- @Ethan: can you flip LRU-prefetch off on canary-3? (ETA 15m)
- @Priya: can you wrap sticky routing flag for canary and run smoke?

End of morning dump. Will iterate after repro run.

-- Amara
